title: Calcium Phosphate Product
description: Calculates the calcium-phosphate product used in renal risk assessment for vascular calcification.
purpose: Used to calculates the calcium-phosphate product used in renal risk assessment for vascular calcification.

advice: An elevated calcium-phosphate product (> 55 mg²/dL²) is associated with an increased risk of vascular calcification and cardiovascular morbidity.
This product is particularly important to monitor in patients with chronic kidney disease and those on dialysis.
warnings: This should be interpreted with the patient's renal and mineral metabolism status.
Treat phosphate elevation rather than calcium alone to reduce the calcium-phosphate product.
followUp: If elevated, assess dietary phosphorus intake and consider phosphate binders.
Monitor parathyroid hormone (PTH) and vitamin D levels in CKD patients.

faq.question: What does an elevated calcium-phosphate product mean?
faq.answer: A product > 55 mg²/dL² indicates an increased risk of metastatic calcification and vascular calcification, especially in CKD patients.

faq.question: How do you lower the calcium-phosphate product?
faq.answer: Reduce dietary phosphorus, use phosphate binders, and optimize dialysis adequacy. Avoid excessive calcium-based binders.

evidence: KDIGO CKD-MBD Guideline. Improving global outcomes (KDIGO) CKD-MBD update. Kidney Int Suppl. 2017;7:1-59.
